cause.summary: CaseStore and Mastra storage opened separate local libSQL clients for one SQLite file. CaseStore configured a 30-second native busy wait and LocalRuntime.seed wrote fixtures for every tool call. If a Mastra interactive transaction held the write lock, the app client synchronously blocked Node before the lock holder's pending commit could run; repeated seeding made this window frequent. The app-only queue in the first attempt did not coordinate Mastra's separate client, which the concurrent duplicate-inbound regression proved with SQLITE_BUSY.
cause.cli_gap: The fixture CLI counted durable effects before entering its reset transaction and deleted local_deliveries. A child process that seeded tenant-a/account-a showed that an earlier test effect written to local-demo was invisible to the guard; the regression now passes the identical tenant/account binding to seed, effect, reset, and a reopened verification connection.

changes: Added a serialized current libSQL client wrapper with zero native busy timeout, bounded cooperative retry, and transaction queue release only after successful commit, rollback, or public close.

Injected the same documented LibSQLStore client into Mastra and CaseStore, so Mastra writes and app-owned interactive transactions use one queue; Mastra owns shared-client shutdown and CaseStore does not close it twice.
Restored WAL after Mastra storage initialization, coalesced successful LocalRuntime fixture seed calls by tenant/account, and catch detached lease-renewal promises.
Made CLI reset guard and fixture deletion one transaction; it preserves local_refunds and local_deliveries and refuses reset when either durable effect exists.

Added deterministic contention, transaction lifecycle, CLI subprocess/reopen, concurrent duplicate-inbound, and recomputed approval-fingerprint regressions. The characterization loader now imports its circular runtime graph serially after module reset.
